definitions.name: 本条局部定义
definitions.body_md: 固定样本x、输入参考r、变量总体N。g(T)=v(x_T)，输出基线b=g(∅)，g0=g−b。

results.original_statement_md:
Specifically, given a pre-trained DNN $v$ and an input sample $\mathbf x=[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ with $n$ variables indexed by $N=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, $v(\mathbf x)\in\mathbb R$ denotes a scalar output of the DNN. Each interaction in [45,27,47] is defined as Harsanyi dividend (or Harsanyi interaction) [18] in game theory, which represents a collaboration (AND relationship) between input variables in a specific set $S$ ($S\subseteq N$). For example, as Figure 1(a) shows, the co-appearance of image patches forms a mouth interaction $S=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$. Only when these three patches are all present, the mouth interaction will be triggered, and make a certain interaction effect $I(S)$ on the network output. The absence (masking) of any patches of $x_1,x_2$, and $x_3$ will deactivate the mouth interaction and remove the interaction effect, i.e., $I(S)=0$. The interaction effect $I(S\mid\mathbf x)$ on the input sample $\mathbf x$ is computed as follows.
$$I(S\mid\mathbf x)=\sum_{T\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|T|}\cdot v(\mathbf x_T).\qquad\text{(1)}$$
where $\mathbf x_T$ denotes the masked input sample, when we mask input variables in $N\setminus T$ and keep variables in $T$ unchanged. Please see more properties of the Harsanyi dividend in the supplementary material.

Footnote 3. Here, $v(\mathbf x)\in\mathbb R$ can be implemented as either a scalar output of the DNN or a dimension of an output vector (e.g., the confidence score of classifying the sample $\mathbf x$ to the ground-truth category $v(\mathbf x)=\log\frac{p(y=y_{truth}\mid\mathbf x)}{1-p(y=y_{truth}\mid\mathbf x)}$).

assumptions: 只需有限集合游戏；不要求可微、不要求稀疏，也不要求输出基线为零。

definitions.name: 本条局部定义
definitions.body_md: 有限总体为 $N$；固定样本、输入基线后，$g(T)=v(x_T)$、$b=g(\varnothing)$，原 $I(S\mid x)$ 对应 $I_g(S)$。$\Omega\subseteq2^N$ 是允许保留的支持族；完整重构可取全部集合，或包含所有非零系数的族。

results.original_statement_md:
Theorem 1. Given an input sample $\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^n$ with $n$ variables, there are $2^n$ different masked samples $\mathbf x_T$ w.r.t. all potential subsets $T\subseteq N$. Then, [45] has proven that

$$\forall T\subseteq N,\quad v(\mathbf x_T)=\sum_{S\subseteq T}I(S\mid\mathbf x)\approx\sum_{S\in\Omega_{\mathrm{salient}}\,\&\,S\subseteq T}I(S\mid\mathbf x).\qquad\text{(3)}$$
results.original_proof_md: Theorem 1 means that we can use a small number of interactive concepts in $\Omega_{\mathrm{salient}}$ to well approximate network outputs on anyone $\mathbf x_T$ of the $2^n$ masked samples.
results.overview: 将定义代入：$\sum_{S\subseteq T}I_g(S)=\sum_{U\subseteq T}g(U)\sum_{U\subseteq S\subseteq T}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}$。内层对差集 $T\setminus U$ 的子集求交替符号和。

proof_steps.title: 交换两层有限子集和
proof_steps.body_md: 将定义代入：$\sum_{S\subseteq T}I_g(S)=\sum_{U\subseteq T}g(U)\sum_{U\subseteq S\subseteq T}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}$。内层对差集 $T\setminus U$ 的子集求交替符号和。

proof_steps.title: 消去真子集并保留空项
proof_steps.body_md: 若 $U\ne T$，内层为 $(1-1)^{|T|-|U|}=0$；若 $U=T$，唯一项为1。因此只剩 $g(T)$。特别地 $I_g(\varnothing)=b$，完整和已经包含输出基线。删除零系数不改变和，但是否只有少量非零项是另一问题。

Removing zero coefficients preserves reconstruction, while having only a few nonzero coefficients is a separate claim.

results.original_statement_md:
Theoretically, there are $2^n$ potential subsets $S$ of input variables ($S\in2^N=\{S\mid S\subseteq N\}$). The proven concept-emergence phenomenon refers to that only a small number of subsets $S\in\Omega_{salient}\subseteq2^N$ make salient interaction effects $I(S\mid\mathbf x)$ on the network output, and can be considered as interactive concepts. Interaction effects of all other subsets are close to zero ($I(S\mid\mathbf x)\approx0$), which can be considered as ignorable noisy patterns. Therefore, the network output $v(\mathbf x)$ can be well approximated by interaction effects of a small number of interactive concepts, i.e.,
$$v(\mathbf x)=\sum_{S\subseteq N}I(S\mid\mathbf x)\approx\sum_{S\in\Omega_{salient}}I(S\mid\mathbf x).\qquad\text{(2)}$$Theorem 1. Given an input sample $\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^n$ with $n$ variables, there are $2^n$ different masked samples $\mathbf x_T$ w.r.t. all potential subsets $T\subseteq N$. Then, [45] has proven that

$$\forall T\subseteq N,\quad v(\mathbf x_T)=\sum_{S\subseteq T}I(S\mid\mathbf x)\approx\sum_{S\in\Omega_{\mathrm{salient}}\,\&\,S\subseteq T}I(S\mid\mathbf x).\qquad\text{(3)}$$

results.original_statement_md:
Ren et al. [45], Li and Zhang [27] have empirically observed and Ren et al. [47] have mathematically proven the counter-intuitive emergence of concepts in DNNs, i.e., it is proven that under a set of common conditions, a DNN encodes just a small number of interactive concepts for inference.We also conduct experiments to illustrate the concept-emergence phenomenon on various DNNs, including multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs), long short-term memory (LSTM), AlexNet [23], ResNet [19], convolutional neural networks (CNNs), and PointNet [41] trained on different types of data, including tabular data (UCI dataset [6]), natural language data (CoLA [61] and SST-2 [56]), image data (MNIST [26] and CelebA [31]), and point cloud data (ShapeNet [65]). We follow experimental settings in [45, 27], and Figure 1(b) shows that interactive concepts encoded by a DNN are usually indeed sparse.

Trustworthiness of interactive concepts. The mathematical proof in [47] makes $I(S)$ become the first concepts whose emergence in DNNs is certificated. Equations (2) and (3) further guarantee that interactive concepts can faithfully explain the output of DNNs. In addition, Li and Zhang [27] have discovered that (i) interactive concepts are transferable across different samples; (ii) interactive concepts are discriminative, i.e., if a concept $S$ has salient interaction effects $I(S)$ on a set of samples, then the concept tends to push these samples to be classified towards the same category. In this way, we can roughly consider such interactive concepts a relatively rigorous definition of concepts.

Complexity (order) of interactive concepts. The complexity of an interactive concept $S$ is defined as the number of input variables involved in $S$, which is also termed the order of the interactive concept, i.e., $\operatorname{complexity}(S)=\operatorname{order}(S)=|S|$. Thus, low-order interactive concepts usually represent simple AND relationships among a few input variables. In comparison, high-order interactive concepts often refer to as relatively complex AND relationships among a large number of input variables.

results.original_statement_md:
Theorem 2 rewrites the Harsanyi interaction effect $I(S\mid\mathbf x)$ of each concept from a new perspective, to facilitate the analysis of the instability of interactive concepts. The derivation of Theorem 2 is inspired by [12, 70, 46], in which the Harsanyi interaction effect is re-written as the sum of the Taylor interaction effects. Therefore, in this study, we define a new baseline value $b_i$ to further extend the finding in [12] and obtain Theorem 2, which significantly simplifies the further proof. Specifically, the new baseline value $b_i$ is set as follows to represent the masked state of the $i$-th input variable. i.e., $x_i\leftarrow b_i$. Previous studies usually set $b_i=\mu_i=\mathbb E_x[x_i]$ as the average value over different samples to represent the masked state [4, 12]. However, we consider that pushing the input variable $x_i$ to move a large distance $\tau\in\mathbb R$ towards $\mu_i$ has been significant enough to remove its information. To this end, we set $b_i=x_i-\tau$ [footnote 4], if $x_i>\mu_i$; else, $b_i=x_i+\tau$ [footnote 4]. The above new setting ensures comparable perturbation magnitudes over different dimensions.

Footnote 4. We need to avoid the case of over-perturbation, by setting $b_i\leftarrow\max(b_i,\mu_i)$ if $x_i>\mu_i$; $b_i\leftarrow\min(b_i,\mu_i)$, otherwise. Fortunately, such cases are uncommon in real applications, so we ignore such settings in the following theoretical analysis.

results.original_statement_md:
3.2 Simple interactive concepts in data are more stable and easier to learn

Unlike other interaction metrics [16, 32, 57], sparse interactive concepts are certificated to emerge in DNN, and can faithfully represent the inference score of DNNs. Therefore, in this study, we aim to further explore the learning difficulty of these certificated concepts. Specifically, we theoretically explain that a DNN is more likely to encode simple (i.e., low-order) interactive concepts.

In this subsection, we show that low-order interactive concepts encoded by DNNs are generally more stable to inevitable noises in data, compared to high-order interactive concepts. Specifically, we derive an approximate analytical solution to the variance (instability) of interactive concepts’ effects w.r.t. data noise, and show that the variance (instability) increases along the order of concepts in an exponential manner.

Theorem 2 (proven in the supplementary material). Given a neural network $v$ and an arbitrary input sample $\mathbf x'\in\mathbb R^n$, the network output can be decomposed by using the Taylor expansion i.e., $v(\mathbf x')=\sum_{S\subseteq N}\sum_{\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S}U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}\cdot J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x')$. In this way, according to Equation (1), the Harsanyi interaction effect $I(S\mid\mathbf x')$ on the sample $\mathbf x'$ can be reformulated as follows.

$$I(S\mid\mathbf x')=\sum_{\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S}U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}\cdot J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x').\qquad\text{(4)}$$

Here, $J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x')=\prod_{i\in S}\left(\operatorname{sign}(x'_i-b_i)\cdot\frac{x'_i-b_i}{\tau}\right)^{\pi_i}$ denotes a Taylor expansion term of the degree $\boldsymbol\pi$, where the degree $\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S=\{[\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_n]\mid\forall i\in S,\pi_i\in\mathbb N^+;\forall i\notin S,\pi_i=0\}$ and $b_i$ is the baseline value to mask the input variable $x_i$. In addition, $U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}=\frac{\tau^m}{\prod_{i=1}^n\pi_i!}\frac{\partial^m v(\mathbf x'_\varnothing)}{\partial x_1^{\pi_1}\cdots\partial x_n^{\pi_n}}\cdot\prod_{i\in S}[\operatorname{sign}(x'_i-b_i)]^{\pi_i}$, where $\mathbf x'_\varnothing$ denotes the sample whose input variables are all masked. $m=\sum_{i=1}^n\pi_i$.

Theorem 2. Given a neural network $v$ and an arbitrary input sample $\mathbf x'\in\mathbb R^n$, the network output can be decomposed by using the Taylor expansion [10], i.e., $v(\mathbf x')=\sum_{S\subseteq N}\sum_{\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S}U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}\cdot J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x')$. In this way, according to Eq. (1), the interaction effect $I(S\mid\mathbf x')$ on the sample $\mathbf x'$ can be reformulated as follows.

$$I(S\mid\mathbf x')=\sum_{\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S}U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}\cdot J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x').\qquad\text{(2)}$$

Here, $J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x')=\prod_{i\in S}(\operatorname{sign}(x'_i-b_i)\cdot\frac{x'_i-b_i}\tau)^{\pi_i}$ denotes a Taylor expansion term of the degree $\boldsymbol\pi$, where the degree $\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S=\{[\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_n]\mid\forall i\in S,\pi_i\in\mathbb N^+;\forall i\notin S,\pi_i=0\}$ and $b_i$ is the baseline value to mask the input variable $x_i$. In addition, $U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}=\frac{\tau^m}{\prod_{i=1}^n\pi_i!}\frac{\partial^m v(\mathbf x'_\varnothing)}{\partial x_1^{\pi_1}\cdots\partial x_n^{\pi_n}}\cdot\prod_{i\in S}[\operatorname{sign}(x'_i-b_i)]^{\pi_i}$, where $\mathbf x'_\varnothing$ denotes the sample whose input variables are all masked. $m=\sum_{i=1}^n\pi_i$.
results.original_proof_md:
Proof. Let us denote the function on the right of Eq. (2) by $\widetilde I(S\mid\mathbf x')$, i.e.,

$$\widetilde I(S\mid\mathbf x')=\sum_{\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S}U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x').\qquad\text{(3)}$$

We need to prove that for any arbitrary input sample $\forall\mathbf x'\in\mathbb R^n,\widetilde I(S\mid\mathbf x')=I(S\mid\mathbf x')$.

Actually, it has been proven in [16] and [45] that the Harsanyi dividend $I(S\mid\mathbf x')$ is the unique metric satisfying the faithfulness requirement mentioned in the main paper, i.e., satisfying

$$\forall T\subseteq N,\quad v(\mathbf x'_T)=\sum_{S\in\Omega,S\subseteq T}I(S\mid\mathbf x').\qquad\text{(4)}$$

Thus, as long as we can prove that $\widetilde I(S\mid\mathbf x')$ also satisfies the above faithfulness requirement, we can obtain $\widetilde I(S\mid\mathbf x')=I(S\mid\mathbf x')$.

To this end, we only need to prove $\widetilde I(S\mid\mathbf x')$ also satisfies the faithfulness requirement in Eq. (4). Specifically, given an input sample $\forall\mathbf x'\in\mathbb R^n$, let us consider the Taylor expansion of the network output $v(\mathbf x_T)$ of an arbitrarily masked sample $\mathbf x'_T$ ($T\subseteq N$), which is expanded at $\mathbf x'_\varnothing=[b_1,\ldots,b_n]$.

Then, we have

$$\forall T\subseteq N,\quad v(\mathbf x'_T)=\sum_{\pi_1=0}^{\infty}\sum_{\pi_2=0}^{\infty}\cdots\sum_{\pi_n=0}^{\infty}\frac1{\prod_{i=1}^n\pi_i!}\frac{\partial^m v(\mathbf x'_\varnothing)}{\partial x_1^{\pi_1}\cdots\partial x_n^{\pi_n}}\cdot\prod_{i=1}^n[(\mathbf x'_T)_i-b_i]^{\pi_i}.\qquad\text{(5)}$$

where $\boldsymbol\pi\in\{[\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_n]\mid\forall i\in N,\pi_i\in\mathbb N\}$ denotes the degree vector of Taylor expansion terms, and $m=\sum_{i=1}^n\pi_i$. In addition, $b_i$ denotes the reference value to mask the input variable $x_i$.

According to the definition of the masked sample $\mathbf x'_T$, we have that all variables in $T$ keep unchanged and other variables are masked to the reference value. That is, $\forall i\in T,(\mathbf x'_T)_i=x_i;\forall i\notin T,(\mathbf x'_T)_i=b_i$. Hence, we obtain $\forall i\notin T,[(\mathbf x'_T)_i-b_i]^{\pi_i}=0$. Then, among all Taylor expansion terms, only terms corresponding to degrees $\boldsymbol\pi$ in the set $P=\{[\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_n]\mid\forall i\in T,\pi_i\in\mathbb N;\forall i\notin T,\pi_i=0\}$ may not be zero. Therefore, Eq. (5) can be rewritten as

$$\forall T\subseteq N,\quad v(\mathbf x'_T)=\sum_{\boldsymbol\pi\in P}\frac1{\prod_{i=1}^n\pi_i!}\frac{\partial^m v(\mathbf x'_\varnothing)}{\partial x_1^{\pi_1}\cdots\partial x_n^{\pi_n}}\cdot\prod_{i\in T}(x'_i-b_i)^{\pi_i}.\qquad\text{(6)}$$

We find that the set $P$ can be divided into multiple disjoint sets as follows, $P=\bigcup_{S\subseteq T}Q_S$, where $Q_S=\{[\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_n]\mid\forall i\in S,\pi_i\in\mathbb N^+;\forall i\notin S,\pi_i=0\}$. Then, we can derive that

$$\begin{aligned}
\forall T\subseteq N,\quad v(\mathbf x'_T)&=\sum_{S\subseteq T}\sum_{\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S}\frac1{\prod_{i=1}^n\pi_i!}\frac{\partial^m v(\mathbf x'_\varnothing)}{\partial x_1^{\pi_1}\cdots\partial x_n^{\pi_n}}\cdot\prod_{i\in S}(x'_i-b_i)^{\pi_i}\\
&=\sum_{S\subseteq T}\sum_{\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S}\underbrace{\frac{\tau^m}{\prod_{i=1}^n\pi_i!}\frac{\partial^m v(\mathbf x'_\varnothing)}{\partial x_1^{\pi_1}\cdots\partial x_n^{\pi_n}}\prod_{i\in S}(\delta_i)^{\pi_i}}_{\text{termed }U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}}\cdot\underbrace{\prod_{i\in S}\left(\delta_i\frac{x'_i-b_i}\tau\right)^{\pi_i}}_{\text{termed }J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x')}.\quad\text{(7)}
\end{aligned}$$

where $\tau\in\mathbb R$ is a pre-defined constant and $\delta_i=\operatorname{sign}(x_i-r_i)\in\{-1,1\}$ is a sign function satisfying $\delta_i^{2m}=1$ ($m=\sum_{i=1}^n\pi_i$). Then, Eq. (7) can be re-written as

$$\forall T\subseteq N,\quad v(\mathbf x'_T)=\sum_{S\subseteq T}\sum_{\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S}U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}\cdot J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x')=\sum_{S\subseteq T}\widetilde I(S\mid\mathbf x').\qquad\text{(8)}$$

Thus, $\widetilde I(S\mid\mathbf x')$ satisfies the faithfulness requirement in Eq. (4) when $\Omega=2^N$.

Therefore, Theorem 2 holds.

proof_steps.title: 按单项式支持重构
proof_steps.body_md: 对于有限多项式，单项式 $m_\pi(z^T)$ 在 $\operatorname{supp}\pi\subseteq T$ 时等于 $m_\pi(z)$，否则有一个正次数零因子，值为0。将同支持的多个次数分别累加，得到 $g(T)=\sum_{S\subseteq T}K_S$。有限 Möbius 唯一性给 $K_S=I_g(S)$，空支持常数也保留。PolynomialSupport 的有限索引允许同一支持有多个不同次数。

en.title: Taylor support expansion and the arbitrary-DNN scope
en.overview: Take the allowed one-dimensional ReLU network $v(t)=\max(t-1/2,0)$, baseline $r=0$ and input $x=1$. Every classical Taylor coefficient at zero vanishes, yet $I_g(\{1\})=v(1)-v(0)=1/2$. Thus the unrestricted global expansion fails for arbitrary DNNs. This is a complete human-readable network counterexample; the machine evidence does not formalize the ReLU counterexample.
assumptions: Retain the source quantifier over arbitrary neural networks. The valid finite component concerns an actual finite polynomial. An infinite series also needs convergence at all relevant masks and legitimate regrouping, which the source does not supply.

definitions.name: Local definitions for this entry
definitions.body_md: The input baseline is $r$, increments are $z_i=x_i-r_i$, and $\pi\in\mathbb N^N$ has support $\{i:\pi_i>0\}$. Set $a_\pi=D^\pi v(r)/\pi!$. Source $U_{S,\pi}(x\prime)$ contains moving signs, while $J$ uses absolute increments; their product is the signed monomial.

proof_steps.title: Reconstruct by monomial support
proof_steps.body_md: For a finite polynomial, $m_\pi(z^T)$ is nonzero only when $\operatorname{supp}\pi\subseteq T$, in which case it equals $m_\pi(z)$; otherwise a positive-degree factor is zero. Grouping every degree at its support gives $g(T)=\sum_{S\subseteq T}K_S$. Möbius uniqueness yields $K_S=I_g(S)$, retaining the empty constant. PolynomialSupport uses a finite term index, allowing several degrees with the same support.

results.original_statement_md:
Next, we analyze the variance (instability) of the interaction effect $I(S\mid\mathbf x'=\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)$ when we add a Gaussian perturbation $\boldsymbol\epsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2 I)$ to the input sample $\mathbf x$. Here, the Gaussian perturbation $\boldsymbol\epsilon\in\mathbb R^n$ is considered as a rough representation of inevitable variations in data, e.g., shape deformation and object rotation variations in image classification. However, such variations are quite difficult to formulate, so we use a Gaussian perturbation as a rough representation. Fortunately, we find that our reformulation of interactions in Theorem 2 enables us to directly apply the finding in [46] to prove the variance (instability) of the interaction effect $I(S\mid\mathbf x'=\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)$.

Theorem 3. Let us add a Gaussian perturbation $\boldsymbol\epsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2 I)$ to the input sample $\mathbf x$. Let us first consider the case with the lowest degree $\widehat{\boldsymbol\pi}=[\widehat\pi_1,\ldots,\widehat\pi_n]\in Q_S$, satisfying that $\forall i\in S,\widehat\pi_i=1;\forall i\notin S,\widehat\pi_i=0$. The mean and variance of $J(S,\widehat{\boldsymbol\pi}\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)$ over the Gaussian perturbation $\boldsymbol\epsilon$ are given as

$$\mathbb E_\epsilon[J(S,\widehat{\boldsymbol\pi}\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]=1,\quad\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[J(S,\widehat{\boldsymbol\pi}\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]=\left(1+\left(\frac\sigma\tau\right)^2\right)^{|S|}-1.\qquad\text{(5)}$$

results.original_statement_md:
Theorem 3. Let us add a Gaussian perturbation $\boldsymbol\epsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2I)$ to the input sample $\mathbf x$. Let us first consider the case with the lowest degree $\widehat{\boldsymbol\pi}=[\hat\pi_1,\ldots,\hat\pi_n]\in Q_S$, satisfying that $\forall i\in S,\hat\pi_i=1;\forall i\notin S,\hat\pi_i=0$. The mean and variance of $J(S,\widehat{\boldsymbol\pi}\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)$ over the Gaussian perturbation $\boldsymbol\epsilon$ are given as

$$\mathbb E_\epsilon[I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]=U_{S,\widehat{\boldsymbol\pi}},\qquad\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]=U_{S,\widehat{\boldsymbol\pi}}^2\left[\left(1+(\sigma/\tau)^2\right)^s-1\right].$$
results.overview: 在掩码 $T$ 下，$g(T)=b+a\prod_i\mathbf1_{i\in T}(x_i-r_i)$；非空完整支持的交互为 $a\prod_i(x_i-r_i)$，常数 $b$ 只贡献空交互。因此加入噪声后的真实交互是 $I_\epsilon=a\prod_i(s_i\tau+\epsilon_i)=U_{ref}\prod_i(1+s_i\epsilon_i/\tau)$。这个有符号恒等式对全部 Gaussian 尾部精确成立，越界时单项式符号与原移动 $U$ 的符号相消。

en.title: The appendix G.2 lowest-I variant and its actual moments
en.overview: At mask $T$, $g(T)=b+a\prod_i\mathbf1_{i\in T}(x_i-r_i)$. Its nonempty full-support dividend is $a\prod_i(x_i-r_i)$; the constant $b$ contributes only the empty dividend. Thus the actual perturbed dividend is $I_\epsilon=a\prod_i(s_i\tau+\epsilon_i)=U_{ref}\prod_i(1+s_i\epsilon_i/\tau)$. This signed identity holds throughout the full Gaussian tails, with the monomial signs canceling the signs in the source moving $U$ coefficient.
assumptions: Use finite support. The nonempty branch is an actual lowest monomial with τ≠0 and measurable independent ε_i∼N(0,σ²). The empty branch has fixed-reference empty-mask output b. Arbitrary-DNN higher terms and the source moving-U notation are not silently removed.

definitions.name: Local definitions for this entry
definitions.body_md: On PDF18, G.2 prose still names $J$, whereas the display uses $I$ and $U_{S,\widehat\pi}$, unlike main PDF5 Eq. (5)’s J moments. Define the actual lowest-support monomial $v(z)=b+a\prod_{i\in S}(z_i-r_i)$ for nonempty $S$, with arbitrary output baseline $b$. Fix $x_i-r_i=s_i\tau$, $s_i\in\{-1,1\}$ and the reference coefficient $U_{ref}=a\prod_i s_i\tau$.

proof_steps.title: Extract the lowest dividend from the actual masked monomial
proof_steps.body_md: At mask $T$, $g(T)=b+a\prod_i\mathbf1_{i\in T}(x_i-r_i)$. Its nonempty full-support dividend is $a\prod_i(x_i-r_i)$; the constant $b$ contributes only the empty dividend. Thus the actual perturbed dividend is $I_\epsilon=a\prod_i(s_i\tau+\epsilon_i)=U_{ref}\prod_i(1+s_i\epsilon_i/\tau)$. This signed identity holds throughout the full Gaussian tails, with the monomial signs canceling the signs in the source moving $U$ coefficient.

proof_steps.title: Compute actual Gaussian moments and delimit the source notation
proof_steps.body_md: Each factor has mean $1$ and second moment $1+\sigma^2/\tau^2$. The actual Gaussian law, L2 integrability and independence yield $EI_\epsilon=U_{ref}$ and $\operatorname{Var}I_\epsilon=U_{ref}^2[(1+\sigma^2/\tau^2)^{|S|}-1]$. The maskedLowest adapter reuses the shared Gaussian integral proof. If G.2’s $U_{S,\widehat\pi}$ denotes the fixed reference $U_{ref}$ and only the lowest term is retained, this proves its displayed formula exactly. Its moving-$x\prime$ definition and higher-order truncation scope for the complete $I$ are not discharged by that type. The main-text $J$ counterexample does not directly refute this signed-$I$ clause. Empty support has its own branch: its fixed-reference empty mask does not vary with noise, so $I_\epsilon(\varnothing)=v(r)=b$, with mean $b$ and variance $0$. Interpreting the source empty-multiindex coefficient $U_{\varnothing,0}$ as the full baseline $v(r)$ makes the displayed formula hold there too, without assuming $b=0$.

assumptions: 独立与L2用于正确乘积矩；反例只有一个Gaussian因子，独立条件自动成立。

definitions.name: 本条局部定义
definitions.body_md: 顶部公式保留作者主张；下面明确分开反例、有效子句及独立修正恒等式。X_i为独立、具有有限二阶矩的实随机变量；原Proposition1在括号内印的是Var[X_i]²，原式原样保留。

results.original_statement_md: Proposition 1. If random variables $X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_k$ are independent of each other, then $\mathbb E[X_1X_2\cdots X_k]=\prod_{i=1}^k\mathbb E[X_i]$, and $\operatorname{Var}[X_1X_2\cdots X_k]=\prod_{i=1}^k(\mathbb E[X_i]^2+\operatorname{Var}[X_i]^2)-\prod_{i=1}^k\mathbb E[X_i]^2$.

results.original_statement_md: Theorem 3 shows the (variance) instability of interactive concepts of different complexities (orders) w.r.t. data variations. It indicates that the variance of $J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)$ roughly increases along with the $\operatorname{order}(S)=|S|$ in an exponential manner. Similar conclusions are also introduced in [70].
results.original_proof_md: Furthermore, according to Equation (4), the interaction effect $I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)$ of the concept $S$ can be represented as the weighted sum of $J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)$, and coefficients $U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}$ w.r.t. different orders $s$ and degrees $\boldsymbol\pi$ are usually chaotic. Hence, we can roughly consider that the variance (instability) of the interaction effect $I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)$ increases along with the order $|S|$ exponentially, as well. In other words, compared to high-order concepts, low-order concepts are much more stable to slight input perturbations.

results.original_statement_md:
Experimental verification. Here, we conduct experiments to verify whether the variance (instability) of interaction effects indeed increased along with the order in an approximately exponential manner. Specifically, to mimic variations in the data, we add Gaussian perturbations $\boldsymbol\epsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,0.02^2I)$ to each training sample. Then, we compute the average mean $E^{(s)}=\mathbb E_{x\in X}[\mathbb E_{S\subseteq N,|S|=s}[|\mathbb E_\epsilon[I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]|]]$ and the average variance $V^{(s)}=\mathbb E_{x\in X}[\mathbb E_{S\subseteq N,|S|=s}[\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]]]$ of interaction effects of the $s$-th order concepts w.r.t. Gaussian perturbations. For verification, we calculate such metrics on DNNs trained for image classification and DNNs trained on tabular data. We train AlexNet [23], VGG-11 [55], ResNet-18/20 [19] on the CIFAR-10 dataset [22] and the Tiny-ImageNet dataset [25], respectively. We also train a five-layer MLP [45] on the UCI census dataset (namely census dataset) and the UCI TV news dataset (namely TV news dataset) [6], respectively. In addition, considering the computational cost of $I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)$ in Equation (1) is intolerable if each pixel is considered as an input variable, we divide images into $8\times8$ patches [45] to calculate $I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)$. Please see the supplementary material for more implementation details.

Figure 2 shows that the variance (instability) $V^{(s)}$ of interaction effects increases in an exponential manner along with the order $s$ of the interactive concept. In addition, the relative stability $E^{(s)}/\sqrt{V^{(s)}}$ of interaction effects decreases significantly along with the order $s$. Such phenomenon successfully verifies findings in Theorem 3.

Figure 2: The logarithm of the variance of interaction effects $\log[V^{(s)}]$ and the stability of interaction effects (measured by $E^{(s)}/\sqrt{V^{(s)}}$). The variance $V^{(s)}$ of interaction effects increases along with the order of interactive concepts exponentially. The stability of effects decreases along with the order.

results.original_statement_md:
3.2.1 Formulating the conceptual learning as a linear regression problem

Note that, Li and Zhang [27] have discovered that interactive concepts have high transferability over samples in the same category, i.e., most interactive concepts extracted from different samples may all belong to the same subset $\Omega_c\subseteq\Omega_{\mathrm{salient}}$. Therefore, we can consider the interactive concepts as common knowledge learned by the DNN, and we aim to analyze the difficulty of learning each interactive concept with different complexity.

To facilitate the analysis, we first simplify the conceptual learning as a linear regression problem. Specifically, we first rewrite the interaction effect of an interactive concept $S$. Given an input sample $\mathbf x$, according to Equation (4), the interaction effect of the concept $S$ on the sample $\mathbf x'$ (obtained by applying some transformations on $\mathbf x$), $I(S\mid\mathbf x')$, can be rewritten as

$$I(S\mid\mathbf x')=U_S\cdot C_S(\mathbf x').\qquad\text{(7)}$$

where the constant $U_S=I(S\mid\mathbf x)$ denotes the interaction effect on the sample $\mathbf x$, and the function for the triggering state on the transformed sample $\mathbf x'$ is given as $C_S(\mathbf x')=\sum_{\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S}U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x')/U_S$.

results.original_statement_md:
Theorem 4. Given an arbitrarily masked sample $\mathbf x_T$ ($T\subseteq N$), the function $C_S(\mathbf x_T)$ defined above can be computed as the binary triggering state of the concept $S$ in the sample $\mathbf x_T$.

$$\forall T\subseteq N,\quad C_S(\mathbf x_T)=\prod_{i\in S}A_i(\mathbf x_T)=\mathbf1(S\subseteq T),\qquad\text{(8)}$$

where $A_i(\mathbf x_T)\in\{0,1\}$ denotes whether the variable $x_i$ is present $A_i(\mathbf x_T)=1$ or being masked $A_i(\mathbf x_T)=0$ in the sample $\mathbf x_T$.

Theorem 4. Given an arbitrarily masked sample $\mathbf x_T$ ($\forall T\subseteq N$), the function $C_S(\mathbf x_T)$ defined above can well fit the binary activation state of the concept $S$ in the sample $\mathbf x_T$.

$$\forall T\subseteq N,\quad C(S\mid\mathbf x_T)=\prod_{i\in S}A_i(\mathbf x_T)=\mathbf1(S\subseteq T).\qquad\text{(19)}$$

where $A_i(\mathbf x_T)\in\{0,1\}$ denotes whether the variable $x_i$ is present $A_i(\mathbf x_T)=1$ or being masked $A_i(\mathbf x_T)=0$ in the sample $\mathbf x_T$.
results.original_proof_md:
The function $C_S(\mathbf x_T)$ represents the triggering state of the concept $S$ under an arbitrarily masking condition $\forall T\subseteq N$. Only when all variables in $S$ are present under the masking condition $T$, the concept $S$ is triggered $C_S(\mathbf x_T)=1$. If any of variables in $S$ is masked, then the concept $S$ will not be triggered $C_S(\mathbf x_T)=0$, yielding zero interaction effect $I(S\mid\mathbf x_T)=0$. Theorem 4 shows that given a masked sample $\mathbf x_T$, the concept $S$ is only triggered when the sample $\mathbf x_T$ contains all variables in $S$, i.e., $T\supseteq S$.

Proof. We know that the function of the activation state on an arbitrary sample $\mathbf x'$ is given by

$$\begin{aligned}
C_S(\mathbf x')&=\sum_{\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S}U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x')/U_S,\\
\text{where }J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x')&=\prod_{i\in S}\left(\operatorname{sign}(x'_i-b_i)\cdot\frac{x'_i-b_i}\tau\right)^{\pi_i}.\quad\text{(20)}
\end{aligned}$$

Specifically, now we consider a masked sample $\mathbf x_T$, and we will prove that $C_S(\mathbf x_T)=\mathbf1(S\subseteq T)$. We consider the following two cases.

Case 1: $S\subsetneq T$. Then there exists some $j\in S\setminus T$. Since $j\notin T$, according to the masking rule of the sample $\mathbf x_T$, we have $(\mathbf x_T)_j-b_j=0$. Since $j\in S$, we have

$$\forall\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S,\quad J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x_T)=\prod_{i\in S}\left(\operatorname{sign}((\mathbf x_T)_i-r_i)\cdot\frac{(\mathbf x_T)_i-b_i}\tau\right)^{\pi_i}=0.\qquad\text{(21)}$$

In this way, we have $C_S(\mathbf x_T)=\sum_{\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S}U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x_T)/U_S=0$.

Case 2: $S\subseteq T$. In this case, $\forall i\in S$, we have $i\in T$. According to the setting of the reference value in Section 2.3 of the main paper, we have $(\mathbf x_T)_i-b_i\in\{\tau,-\tau\}$. Then we have $\operatorname{sign}((\mathbf x_T)_i-b_i)\cdot\frac{(\mathbf x_T)_i-b_i}\tau=1,\forall i\in S$. This further implies that

$$\forall\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S,\quad J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x_T)=\prod_{i\in S}\left(\operatorname{sign}((\mathbf x_T)_i-b_i)\cdot\frac{(\mathbf x_T)_i-b_i}\tau\right)^{\pi_i}=1.\qquad\text{(22)}$$

Therefore, we can derive

$$C_S(\mathbf x_T)=\sum_{\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S}U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}/U_S.\qquad\text{(23)}$$

Recall that $U_S=I(S\mid\mathbf x)=\sum_{\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S}U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x)$, in which $J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x)=\prod_{i\in S}(\operatorname{sign}(x_i-r_i)\cdot\frac{x_i-b_i}\tau)^{\pi_i}=1$, because $x_i-b_i\in\{\tau,-\tau\}$. So actually, we have

$$U_S=\sum_{\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S}U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}.\qquad\text{(24)}$$

Therefore, $C_S(\mathbf x_T)=\sum_{\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S}U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}/U_S=1$.

Combining the two cases, we can conclude that $C_S(\mathbf x_T)=\mathbf1(S\subseteq T)=\prod_{i\in S}A_i(\mathbf x_T)$.

results.original_statement_md:
Thus, inspired by [46], we can extend the conclusion to a continuous version that explains the output of the DNN as a linear regression of very few salient interactive concepts based on Equation (3).

$$v(\mathbf x')=\sum_{S\subseteq N}U_S\cdot C_S(\mathbf x')\approx\sum_{S\in\Omega_{\mathrm{salient}}}U_S\cdot C_S(\mathbf x').\qquad\text{(9)}$$
results.original_proof_md:
where the triggering state $C_S(\mathbf x')$ of each interactive concept $S$ can be considered as an input dimension of the linear function, which reflects whether the input sample $\mathbf x'$ contains the concept $S$.

Therefore, the absolute value of the weight coefficient $U_S$ in Equation (9) can be viewed as the strength of the DNN encoding the interactive concept $S$. Considering the sparsity of interactive concepts discussed in Section 3.1, most interactive concepts have ignorable coefficients $U_S\approx0$, and not so many concepts $S$ have large absolute value of $|U_S|$. Thus, we can consider that the DNN only learns a small number of salient interactive concepts.

results.original_statement_md:
3.2.2 Explaining the learning difficulty of concepts

Equation (9) in the previous subsection enables us to understand a DNN for the classification task as a pseudo-linear function. Then, if an input feature dimension has a stable value (i.e., the triggering state $C_S$ of an interactive concept $S$ stably being present/absent) across all samples in the same category, then we consider this feature dimension (i.e., the concept) is easy to learn. In comparison, when we extract the same concept from different samples in the same category, if this concept exhibits inconsistent interaction effects (e.g., such a concept does not consistently present or absent over different samples), then this feature dimension (i.e., the concept) is hard to learn.
results.original_proof_md: To analyze the consistency/stability of the concept w.r.t data variations, we use small perturbations $\boldsymbol\epsilon$ to represent various inevitable variations in the data, such as shape deformation and object rotation variations. Theorem 3 shows that high-order interactive concepts are much more unstable to inevitable variations in the data than low-order interactive concepts. This makes high-order concepts more likely to be influenced by data variations and less likely to be consistently present or absent in samples of the same category, which boosts the learning difficulty.

results.original_statement_md:
Experimental verification. We conduct experiments to verify the claim that high-order interactive concepts are less stably extracted under data variations than low-order interaction. We use the following two metrics to evaluate the each interactive concept $S$ (i.e., each single input dimension of the above linear function) of a certain order. Specifically, we use the first metric $\beta(S)=\mathbb E_c\left[|\mathbb E_{x\in X_c}[I(S\mid\mathbf x)]|/\operatorname{Std}_{x\in X_c}[I(S\mid\mathbf x)]\right]$ to measure the relative consistency of the interactive concept appearing over different input samples in a certain category $c$. Here, $X_c$ denotes a set of training samples belonging to the category $c$, and $\operatorname{Std}_{x\in X_c}[I(S\mid\mathbf x)]$ indicates the standard deviation of $I(S\mid\mathbf x)$ over different input samples. A large $\beta(S)$ value means that the interactive concept $S$ in all samples of the category $c$ has similar/consistent effects $I(S\mid\mathbf x)$. It is easier for a DNN to learn such a consistent concept $S$.

In addition, we use another metric $\kappa(S)$ to verify whether the interaction effect of the high-order interactive concept is usually less stably extracted than those of the low-order interactive concept. To this end, the metric $\kappa(S)=\mathbb E_{x\in X}[\mathbb E_\epsilon[|I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)-I(S\mid\mathbf x)|]]/\mathbb E_{x\in X}[|I(S\mid\mathbf x)|]=\mathbb E_{x\in X}[\mathbb E_\epsilon[|C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)-C_S(\mathbf x)|]]/\mathbb E_{x\in X}[|C_S(\mathbf x)|]$ measures the relative instability of the interactive concept $S$ to the inevitable slight variations $\boldsymbol\epsilon$ in the data. Here, $C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)=I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)/U_S$ computed in Equation (7) denotes the trigger state of the interactive concept $S$ on the sample $\mathbf x'=\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon$.

To this end, we use DNNs and experimental settings in the experimental verification paragraph of Section 3.2 for evaluation. Figure 3 and Figure 4 show the change of the average consistency $\beta(S)$ and the average instability $\kappa(S)$ of $s$-order interactive concepts through the learning process, respectively. At each training epoch, low-order concepts usually obtain higher consistency $\beta(S)$ and lower instability $\kappa(S)$ than high-order concepts. It means that low-order concepts usually are more consistent and more stable. Thus, this experiment explains the reason why low-order interactive concepts are easier to learn.

Figure 3: Consistency $\beta(S)$ of $s$-order interactive concepts. The curve shows the mean consistency $\mathbb E_{S\subseteq N,|S|=s}[\beta(S)]$ over different interactive concepts of the $s$-th order, and the shade indicates the standard deviation $\operatorname{Std}_{S\subseteq N,|S|=s}[\beta(S)]$. Effects of low-order concepts are more consistent than those of high-order concepts.

Figure 4: Instability $\kappa(S)$ of $s$-order interactive concepts to data variations. The curve shows the average instability $\mathbb E_{S\subseteq N,|S|=s}[\kappa(S)]$ over different interactive concepts of the $s$-th order, and the shade represents the standard deviation $\operatorname{Std}_{S\subseteq N,|S|=s}[\kappa(S)]$. Effects of high-order concepts are more sensitive to data variations than those of low-order concepts.

The definition of the interaction function $v_T$ parameterized by a subset of variables $T$ is given as follows. $\forall S\subseteq N$, if $T\subseteq S$, $v_T(S)=c$; otherwise, $v_T(S)=0$. results.original_statement_md:
F. Complexity of interactive concepts.
Many previous studies [11,67,59,45,43] used multi-order interactions to analyze DNNs. Specifically, Given a pre-trained DNN $v$ and a masked sample $\mathbf x_S$, the multi-order interaction $I^{(m)}(i,j)$ used in [59,11,67] is given as follows:
$$I^{(m)}(i,j)=\mathbb E_{S\subseteq N\setminus\{i,j\},|S|=m}[\Delta v(i,j,S)].\qquad\text{(1)}$$
where $\Delta v(i,j,S)=v(\mathbf x_{S\cup\{i,j\}})-v(\mathbf x_{S\cup\{i\}})-v(\mathbf x_{S\cup\{j\}})+v(\mathbf x_S)$. They consider that $I^{(m)}(i,j)$ reflects the collaboration with $m$ contextual variables ($m$ pixels). In this way, the order $m$ measures the number of variables in $S$. Therefore, a low-order interaction denotes a relatively simple collaboration between input variables with a small context $S$. In contrast, a high-order interaction represents a complex collaboration between input variables with a large context $S$.
In this paper, we consider that the number of variables in an interactive concept $S$ can measure the complexity of an interactive concept encoded by a DNN, namely the order of the interactive concept, $\operatorname{complexity}(S)=\operatorname{order}(S)=|S|$. Thus, low-order concepts usually represent simple AND relationships among a few input variables. In comparison, high-order concepts often refer to as relatively complex AND relationships among a large number of input variables.

results.original_statement_md:
In this section, we derive that high-order interactive concepts (computed via the Harsanyi dividend [18]) can be considered as elementary components for high-order interactions used in [43].

Given a pre-trained DNN $v$ and a masked sample $\mathbf x_S$, the multi-order interaction $I^{(m)}(i,j)$ used in [43] is given as follows:

$$I^{(m)}(i,j)=\mathbb E_{S\subseteq N\setminus\{i,j\},|S|=m}[\Delta v(i,j,S)].\qquad\text{(25)}$$

where $\Delta v(i,j,S)=v(\mathbf x_{S\cup\{i,j\}})-v(\mathbf x_{S\cup\{i\}})-v(\mathbf x_{S\cup\{j\}})+v(\mathbf x_S)$.
results.original_proof_md:
Let $\Delta v_T(S)=\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|L|}v(\mathbf x_{L\cup S})$ denote the marginal benefit of variables in $T\subseteq N\setminus S$, given the environment $S$. In this way, $\Delta v_T(S)$ can be represented as the sum of interaction effects inside $T$ and sub-environments of $S$, i.e. $\Delta v_T(S)=\sum_{S'\subseteq S}I(T\cup S')$ [45].

Thus, the $I^{(m)}(i,j)$ can be represented as follows,

$$\begin{aligned}
I^{(m)}(i,j)&=\mathbb E_{S\subseteq N\setminus\{i,j\},|S|=m}[\Delta v(i,j,S)]\\
&=\mathbb E_{S\subseteq N\setminus\{i,j\},|S|=m}\left[\sum_{L\subseteq S}I(L\cup\{i,j\})\right]\\
&=\frac1{\binom{n-2}{m}}\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq N\setminus\{i,j\}\\|S|=m}}\left[\sum_{L\subseteq S}I(L\cup\{i,j\})\right]\\
&=\sum_{\substack{L\subseteq N\setminus\{i,j\}\\|L|\le m}}I(L\cup\{i,j\})\sum_{\substack{L\subseteq S\subseteq N\setminus\{i,j\}\\|S|=m}}\frac1{\binom{n-2}{m}}\\
&=\sum_{\substack{L\subseteq N\setminus\{i,j\}\\|L|\le m}}I(L\cup\{i,j\})\frac{\binom{n-2}{m-l}}{\binom{n-2}{m}}\\
&=\sum_{l=0}^m\sum_{\substack{L\subseteq N\setminus\{i,j\}\\|L|=m}}\frac{\binom{n-2}{m-l}}{\binom{n-2}{m}}I(L\cup\{i,j\}).
\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, we prove that $I^{(m)}(i,j)=\sum_{l=0}^m\sum_{\substack{L\subseteq N\setminus\{i,j\}\\|L|=m}}\frac{\binom{n-2}{m-l}}{\binom{n-2}{m}}I(L\cup\{i,j\})$.

definitions.body_md: The top formula retains the author’s claim. The steps distinguish counterexamples, valid clauses and separately repaired identities. Let i≠j belong to N, R=N\{i,j}, n=|N| and 0≤m≤n−2. The context cardinality is m, while the concept support size is |L|+2. Define Δg(i,j,S)=g(Sij)−g(Si)−g(Sj)+g(S). The displayed rewrite is the correct relation; original Eq. (25) is retained unchanged.

proof_steps.title: First prove the actual difference decomposition for each context
proof_steps.body_md: Reconstruct the four game values and cancel all terms except those containing i and j. This yields $\Delta g(i,j,S)=\sum_{L\subseteq S}I_g(L\cup\{i,j\})$. Lean derives this from higherMarginal reconstruction and takes the exact average over every size-m context.

proof_steps.title: Count by a bijection, then exchange sums and group by size
proof_steps.body_md: Fix $L\subseteq R$ with $|L|=l\le m$. The map $S\mapsto S\setminus L$ bijects contexts containing $L$ with cardinality $m$ with subsets of $R\setminus L$ having cardinality $(m-l)$; its inverse is $W\mapsto L\cup W$. Thus the multiplicity is $\binom{|R|-l}{m-l}=\binom{n-2-l}{m-l}$. Exchange the two finite sums and group $L$ by cardinality to obtain the separately displayed correct identity below. DifficultyCounting proves the bijection, multiplicities, sum exchange and cardinality grouping; the paper adapter proves $|N\setminus\{i,j\}|=n-2$. Both original errors in Eq. (25) remain unchanged and are refuted in the next step.

proof_steps.title: Refute the final index and combinatorial coefficient separately
proof_steps.body_md: For N={1,2,3}, i=1,j=2,m=1 use the actual masked score v=z1z2 with x=1,r=0. The mean difference is1, while printed |L|=m selects only L={3}, whose three-way dividend is0, giving RHS0. Next take N of size4,m2,v=z1z2z3. The true mean is1. Even after repairing only the inner index, the sole L={3} gets the source coefficient choose(2,1)/choose(2,2)=2, producing RHS2. Both Lean counterexamples use masked coordinate polynomials rather than arbitrarily assigned dividends.

results.title: 真实独立 Gaussian 回归最优与丢均值反例
assumptions: 固定特征分布、平方损失与正真实方差。主反例双方差1，使Σ=Σ²=I，两种原记号读法相同。

definitions.name: 本条局部定义
definitions.body_md: 特征索引为有限集合 $\{1,\ldots,k\}$；$f,w,\mu\in\mathbb R^k$，$d=(d_i)$ 是真实方差向量，$K\in\mathbb R^{k\times k}$。顶部公式保留作者主张；下面明确分开反例、有效子句及独立修正恒等式。f_i独立Gaussian，均值μ_i、真实方差d_i>0。$K=E[ff^\top]=\mu\mu^\top+\operatorname{diag}d$。原文先写N(μ,Σ²)，又写Σ=diag(σ_i²)，与K=μμᵀ+Σ²有方差/方差平方记号冲突。

results.original_statement_md:
There is a close connection between the variance of interactive concepts and the learning difficulty. In fact, a similar connection has been discovered by [46]. The theoretical connection is proved as follows. Specifically, we simplify the learning of a DNN into a linear regression problem. In this very simple setting, we assume each $i$-th concept encoded by the DNN to be a specific feature, and use $f_i$ to represent the triggering (presence) state of the $i$-th concept in a training sample. Because according to Eq. (9) in the main paper, the network output $v(\cdot)$ is the sum of a small number of salient interactive concepts, we roughly simplify and rewrite the inference output of the DNN as the following linear function

$$y=\mathbf w^\top\mathbf f=w_1f_1+\cdots+w_df_d,$$

where $\mathbf f=[f_1,\ldots,f_d]^\top$. Then, $w_i$ can be viewed as the strength of the DNN encoding the $i$-th interactive concept. In this way, if $w_i\approx0$, the DNN does not learn the $i$-th interactive concept.

We suppose that training samples are sampled from $\mathbf f\sim P(\mathbf f)=\mathcal N(\boldsymbol\mu,\Sigma^2)$ and $y^*$ denotes the ground truth label. Specifically, $\boldsymbol\mu=[\mu_1,\mu_2,\ldots,\mu_d]^\top$ and $\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1^2,\sigma_2^2,\ldots,\sigma_d^2)$.

The toy regression problem can be formulated as follows,

$$\mathcal L=\mathbb E_{P(\mathbf f)}\left[\frac12(\mathbf w^\top\mathbf f-y^*)^2\right].\qquad\text{(26)}$$
results.original_proof_md:
We derive the optimal weights to the above regression task in three steps.

Step 1. The optimal weight $w_i$ for the regression problem in Eq. (26) is computed by

$$\forall1\le i\le d,\quad w_i=\frac1{\det K}\det(\mathbf K_1,\ldots,\mathbf K_{i-1},\boldsymbol\zeta,\mathbf K_{i+1},\ldots,\mathbf K_d).\qquad\text{(27)}$$

where $K=\boldsymbol\mu\boldsymbol\mu^\top+\Sigma^2$, $\boldsymbol\zeta=y^*\boldsymbol\mu$, and $\mathbf K_j$ denotes the $j$-th column of the matrix $K$.

Step 2. We further prove that for the optimal $\mathbf w$, we have

$$\forall1\le i,j\le d,\quad\frac{|w_i|}{|w_j|}=\frac{|\mu_i/\sigma_i^2|}{|\mu_j/\sigma_j^2|}.\qquad\text{(28)}$$

Step 3. Based on Step 2, we can derive $|w_i|\propto|1/\sigma_i^2|$, where $w_i$ denotes the strength of the DNN encoding the $i$-th interactive concept. $|w_i|\propto|1/\sigma_i^2|$ indicates that the learning effect of the $i$-th interactive concept is inversely proportional to the variance of the $i$-th interactive concept. Therefore, interactive concepts with high variances (high-order interactive concepts) are more difficult to learn.
results.overview: 原 Eq.(26) 是 $\mathcal L=\frac12 E(w^\top f-y^*)^2$。为调用公共库，令 $L=2\mathcal L$；正因子不改变严格比较或唯一 argmin。两两独立的有限二阶矩特征满足 $L(w)=(y^*-\mu^\top w)^2+\sum_i d_iw_i^2$，因为非对角协方差为零。故 $K=\mu\mu^\top+\operatorname{diag}d$，原半损失的梯度是 $Kw-y^*\mu$。实际 Gaussian 法则证明均值与二阶矩，而不把期望等式放入假设。

proof_steps.body_md: 原 Eq.(26) 是 $\mathcal L=\frac12 E(w^\top f-y^*)^2$。为调用公共库，令 $L=2\mathcal L$；正因子不改变严格比较或唯一 argmin。两两独立的有限二阶矩特征满足 $L(w)=(y^*-\mu^\top w)^2+\sum_i d_iw_i^2$，因为非对角协方差为零。故 $K=\mu\mu^\top+\operatorname{diag}d$，原半损失的梯度是 $Kw-y^*\mu$。实际 Gaussian 法则证明均值与二阶矩，而不把期望等式放入假设。

proof_steps.title: 用正定正规方程连接 Cramer 与闭式最优
proof_steps.body_md: 令 $H=1+\sum_j\mu_j^2/d_j>0$，$w_i^*=y^*\mu_i/(d_iH)$。直接验算 $Kw^*=y^*\mu$。对 $z\ne0$，$z^\top Kz=(\mu^\top z)^2+\sum_i d_iz_i^2>0$，故 $\det K>0$ 且 $L(w)-L(w^*)=(w-w^*)^\top K(w-w^*)>0$。原 Eq.(27) 的换列行列式表达是同一正规方程的 Cramer 解，实际适配已连接该式与唯一最优。比值 $|w_i^*|/|w_j^*|=|\mu_i/d_i|/|\mu_j/d_j|$ 需分母非零；当 $\sigma_i^2$ 表示真实方差 $d_i$ 时，它给原 Step2。若按原 $\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_i^2)$、$\operatorname{Cov}f=\Sigma^2$ 字面读，$d_i=\sigma_i^4$，原 Eq.(28) 亦不能无条件称正确。两种读法都不能从 Step2 删除均值。
proof_steps.formula_tex: \begin{aligned}H&=1+\sum_j\mu_j^2/d_j,\quad w_i^*=y^*\mu_i/(d_iH),\quad Kw^*=y^*\mu,\\\det K&>0,\quad w_i^*=\det(K[i\leftarrow y^*\mu])/\det K,\\L(w)-L(w^*)&=(w-w^*)^\top K(w-w^*)>0\quad(w\ne w^*)\end{aligned}

en.title: Actual independent-Gaussian optimum and the omitted-mean counterexample
en.overview: Source Eq. (26) is $\mathcal L=\frac12 E(w^\top f-y^*)^2$. Set $L=2\mathcal L$ to use the public library; a positive factor preserves strict comparisons and the unique argmin. Pairwise independent features with finite second moments satisfy $L(w)=(y^*-\mu^\top w)^2+\sum_i d_iw_i^2$, since off-diagonal covariances vanish. Therefore $K=\mu\mu^\top+\operatorname{diag}d$ and the source half-loss gradient is $Kw-y^*\mu$. Actual Gaussian laws establish the means and second moments instead of assuming those expectation identities.
assumptions: Fix the feature distribution and squared loss, with positive true variances. Both variances are1 in the main counterexample, so Σ=Σ²=I under either source notation.

definitions.name: Local definitions for this entry
definitions.body_md: Features have finite index $\{1,\ldots,k\}$, with $f,w,\mu\in\mathbb R^k$, true-variance vector $d=(d_i)$ and $K\in\mathbb R^{k\times k}$. The top formula retains the author’s claim. The steps distinguish counterexamples, valid clauses and separately repaired identities. The f_i are independent Gaussian features with means μ_i and true variances d_i>0. K=E[ffᵀ]=μμᵀ+diag d. The source writes N(μ,Σ²), then Σ=diag(σ_i²) and K=μμᵀ+Σ², creating a variance-versus-squared-variance notation conflict.

proof_steps.title: Connect the source half loss to the actual expectation
proof_steps.body_md: Source Eq. (26) is $\mathcal L=\frac12 E(w^\top f-y^*)^2$. Set $L=2\mathcal L$ to use the public library; a positive factor preserves strict comparisons and the unique argmin. Pairwise independent features with finite second moments satisfy $L(w)=(y^*-\mu^\top w)^2+\sum_i d_iw_i^2$, since off-diagonal covariances vanish. Therefore $K=\mu\mu^\top+\operatorname{diag}d$ and the source half-loss gradient is $Kw-y^*\mu$. Actual Gaussian laws establish the means and second moments instead of assuming those expectation identities.

proof_steps.title: Connect Cramer and the closed optimum through positive definite normal equations
proof_steps.body_md: Let $H=1+\sum_j\mu_j^2/d_j>0$ and $w_i^*=y^*\mu_i/(d_iH)$; verify $Kw^*=y^*\mu$. For $z\ne0$, $z^\top Kz=(\mu^\top z)^2+\sum_i d_iz_i^2>0$, so $\det K>0$ and $L(w)-L(w^*)=(w-w^*)^\top K(w-w^*)>0$. The column-replacement determinant in source Eq. (27) is Cramer’s solution of this same normal equation; the actual adapter connects it to the unique optimum. The ratio $|w_i^*|/|w_j^*|=|\mu_i/d_i|/|\mu_j/d_j|$ requires a nonzero denominator and gives source Step2 when $\sigma_i^2$ means the true variance $d_i$. Under the literal notation $\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_i^2)$ and $\operatorname{Cov}f=\Sigma^2$, however, $d_i=\sigma_i^4$ and source Eq. (28) is not generally correct either. Neither reading permits dropping the means.

proof_steps.title: Give a counterexample without covariance-notation ambiguity
proof_steps.body_md: Take independent Gaussians with μ=(1,2), d=(1,1), y*=1. Then K=[[2,2],[2,5]], detK=6 and the unique optimum is (1/6,1/3). The actual ratio is1/2, whereas Step3’s inverse-variance ratio is1. The machine statement binds the actual expected loss on Measure.pi, strict inequality for every other weight vector and the conflicting ratios.

results.original_statement_md:
H. Experimental Settings.
Training details. We trained AlexNet [23], VGG-11 [55], ResNet-18/20 [19] on the CIFAR-10 dataset [22] and the Tiny ImageNet dataset [25], respectively. We also trained a five-layer MLP on the UCI census dataset (namely census dataset) and the UCI TV news dataset (namely TV news dataset) [6], respectively. Each layer of the MLP contained 100 neurons. We trained each neural networks for 200 epochs with the SGD optimizer.
Sampling details. Since, the computational cost of $I(S\mid\mathbf x)$ was intolerable in real implementation, we applied the sampling-based approximation method in [67] to calculate $I(S\mid\mathbf x)$. Due to the high dimension of image data (e.g. $224\times224$ for ImageNet), we uniformly split the input image into $8\times8$ patches. Furthermore, we random sampled 12 patches and considered these patches as input variables for each image. The remaining 52 patches are set to the baseline value.
Implementations details. Here, we introduce how to measure $\beta(S)$ and $\kappa(S)$ in Section 2.3. On the Tiny ImageNet dataset, we randomly sampled 100 training images. These training images were randomly sampled from different 10 classes. On the CIFAR-10 dataset, we randomly sampled 10 training images from each class. For tabular datasets, we randomly sampled 50 training samples from each class. For image datasets, we set $\tau=2$ when the input data is normalized by its standard deviation. For tabular datasets, we set $\tau=1$ when the input data is normalized by its standard deviation. results.original_statement_md: Specifically, we examine whether interactive concepts encoded by the finally-learned DNN $v_{\mathrm{final}}(x)$ have already been encoded by the DNN that is $v_t(x)$ trained after $t$ epochs. If so, we consider such interactive concepts are learned fast. Specifically, let $\mathbf I_t^{(s)}=[I_t(S_1|x),\cdots,I_t(S_d|x)]^\top\in\mathbb R^d$ denote a vector of interaction effects for all $d=\binom ns$ interactive concepts of $s$-order. Then, we compute the Jaccard similarity between $s$-order interactive concepts encoded by the DNN $v_{\mathrm{final}}(x)$ and those encoded by the DNN $v_t(x)$, i.e., $sim(\mathbf I_t^{(s)},\mathbf I_{\mathrm{final}}^{(s)})=\|\min(\widetilde{\mathbf I}_t^{(s)},\widetilde{\mathbf I}_{\mathrm{final}}^{(s)})\|_1/\|\max(\widetilde{\mathbf I}_t^{(s)},\widetilde{\mathbf I}_{\mathrm{final}}^{(s)})\|_1$ and $\|\cdot\|_1$ denotes L1-norm. We extend the $d$-dimensional vector $\mathbf I_t^{(s)}$ into a $2d$-dimensional vector with non-negative elements $\widetilde{\mathbf I}_t^{(s)}=[(\mathbf I_t^{(s),+})^\top,(\mathbf I_t^{(s),-})^\top]^\top=[\max(\mathbf I_t^{(s)},0)^\top,-\min(\mathbf I_t^{(s)},0)^\top]^\top\in\mathbb R^{2d}$. Similarly, we compute $\widetilde{\mathbf I}_{\mathrm{final}}^{(s)}$ with non-negative elements based on $\mathbf I_{\mathrm{final}}^{(s)}$. In this way, a large similarity $sim(\mathbf I_t^{(s)},\mathbf I_{\mathrm{final}}^{(s)})$ at an earlier epoch $t$ indicates that interactive concepts are easier to be learned.

To this end, we use the metric $\alpha(S)=\mathbb E_{x\in X}[|I(S|x+\delta)-I(S|x)|]/\mathbb E_{x\in X}[|I(S|x)|]$ to evaluate the sensitivity of the interactive concept $S$ to adversarial perturbations, where $\delta$ denotes the adversarial perturbation generated by the $\ell_\infty$ attack [33]. Such phenomena demonstrate that low-order interactive concepts are more robust to adversarial attacks.

results.original_statement_md: In this subsection, we illustrate the phenomenon that low-order interactive concepts are usually learned faster than high-order concepts, as a support for the claim that low-order interactive concepts are easier to be learned. We have theoretically proven in Section 3.2 and experimentally verified that low-order interactive concepts are more consistently present or consistently absent in different samples of the same category, which makes low-order interactive concepts easier to be learned. Then, this experiment is conducted to check whether low-order concepts are really learned faster than high-order concepts.
results.original_proof_md:
To this end, let us use DNNs and experimental settings introduced in the experimental verification paragraph of Section 3.2 for evaluation. Figure 5 shows that DNNs first learn low-order interactive concepts, and then learn high-order interactive concepts. Such a phenomenon verifies the conclusion that a DNN easily learns low-order (simple) interactive concepts.

Figure 5: The weighted Jaccard similarity $sim(\mathbf I_t^{(s)},\mathbf I_{\mathrm{final}}^{(s)})$ between $s$-order interactive concepts learned after the intermediate epoch $\mathbf I_t^{(s)}$ and those learned after the final epoch $\mathbf I_{\mathrm{final}}^{(s)}$. Low-order concepts usually have higher Jaccard similarity during the learning process, which indicates that DNNs first learn low-order concepts and then gradually learn more about high-order concepts.

results.original_statement_md: Previous study [43] has discovered that low-order interactions are more robust to adversarial attacks than high-order interactions. Notice that their high-order (low-order) interactions are different from, but highly related to our high-order (low-order) interactive concepts. Specifically, our interactive concepts can be explained as elementary components for such multi-order interactions in [43]. Please see the supplementary material for the proof. Therefore, from this perspective, our conclusion that “low-order interactive concepts are easy to learn” can also explain how a DNN encodes concepts of different adversarial robustness.
results.original_proof_md: Can we use interactive concepts in this paper to verify the heuristic findings of adversarial robustness in [43]? According to Equation (2), we can represent the inference logic of a DNN by a set of interactive concepts, i.e., $v(x)\approx\sum_{S\in\Omega_{\mathrm{salient}}}I(S|x)$. In this way, we conduct experiments to evaluate the sensitivity of each interactive concept $S$ to adversarial perturbations. The symbolic conceptual representation of interactive concepts allows us to measure the adversarial robustness in a more direct way. That is, if the effect of an interactive concept does not significantly change under adversarial attacks, we consider this interactive concept is robust to adversarial attacks. In contrast, if the effect of an interactive concept changes significantly under adversarial attacks, we consider this interactive concept is sensitive to adversarial attacks.

results.original_statement_md:
In this subsection, we discuss some related studies on which kind of knowledge is usually first learned by a DNN. Most previous studies conducted experiments to explore the knowledge that was easier to be learned by a DNN, without providing much theoretical support. However, we find that our theorems can partially explain mechanisms behind some previous findings.

Arpit et al. [5] trained DNNs to classify both normal samples and white-noise samples to different object categories. In this way, they considered that the DNN encoded simple concepts to classify normal samples, but the DNN had to learn complex concepts to classify white noises to randomly-assigned labels. They observed that the DNN usually learned normal samples first, because the classification accuracy of normal samples increased before that of white noises. To this end, our research provides more insights into such an observation. Specifically, Cheng et al. [8] have proven that the classification of noisy data usually depends on high-order concepts, i.e., the classification of noisy data forces the DNN to memorize each specific white-noise sample as a specific high-order interactive concept. Let us combine this conclusion with our finding that high-order interactive concepts are hard to learn. Then, we can easily owe the slow learning of white-noise samples observed in [5] to the difficulty of learning high-order concepts.

definitions.body_md: [34]按SVM/RF能否正确分类定义easy/hard；这不同于支持阶数定义。

results.original_statement_md: Mangalam and Prabhu [34] considered/defined easy samples as training samples that could be correctly classified by shallow machine learning models, such as support vector machine (SVM) and random forests (RF). They discovered that DNNs first learned easy samples, and then gradually learned more about hard samples. To this end, our research verifies such observation. Specifically, we claim that easy samples mainly contain low-order interactive concepts. Thus, hard samples mainly contain high-order interactive concepts corresponding to complex interactions between numerous input variables, and thus are difficult to be classified by shallow models (e.g., the SVM and the RF). In this way, the fast learning of low-order concepts is another understanding of the finding in [34].

results.statement_tex: \text{qualitative source inference; no quantified rate theorem}

definitions.body_md: [63]讨论损失景观/样本空间频率，而F06讨论中间特征二维DFT，两者不同。

results.original_statement_md: Xu et al. [63] discovered that during the training process, DNNs usually first learned samples of low frequencies (e.g., robust to noises), and then encoded samples of high frequencies (e.g., sensitive to noises). However, the original design of DNNs is not towards learning specific spectrums, and techniques of deep learning are not developed by assuming a periodic loss landscape of training samples. Therefore, we believe there should be a more direct explanation for the spectrum-learning phenomenon discovered by [63]. To this end, our research explains this phenomenon as the difficulty of learning high-order concepts. According to Section 4.1, low-order concepts usually are less sensitive to input perturbations, thereby corresponding to low-frequency components defined in the loss landscape in [63]. Accordingly, high-order concepts correspond to high-frequency components.

results.original_statement_md: Liu et al. [28] discovered that during adversarial training, the training loss of the DNN trained on easy samples decreased faster than that of the DNN trained on hard samples. To this end, we consider easy samples in adversarial training mentioned by [28] may mainly contain low-order interactive concepts. It is because, as discussed in Section 4.1, [43] discovered that low-order interactions were robust to adversarial perturbations. Thus, the fast learning of easy samples in adversarial training can be roughly owing to the learning of low-order concepts.

Lean’s total-division identity exists for all m; it represents an actual uniform mean only on m≤|R|.

en.impact_md: The finite-polynomial machine type is not expanded to the original arbitrary-DNN quantifier.

issues.title: 最低阶 J 自身的均值和方差错式
issues.problem_md: 原对象J含绝对增量；小Gaussian不会几乎处处保持符号。
issues.evidence_md: 单支持、τ1、ε~N(0,q),q>0时J=|1+ε|。实际Lean证明EJ>1及VarJ<q，完整原对象、真实法则和两个矩都已绑定。
issues.impact_md: 与F08及本篇G2显示的有符号最低I矩区分；这里只否定正文J精确子句，不由此否定附录I变体。

en.title: Incorrect mean and variance of the lowest J itself
en.problem_md: The original J contains absolute increments; a small Gaussian does not preserve signs almost surely.
en.evidence_md: For one support, τ1 and ε~N(0,q), q>0, J=|1+ε|. Lean proves EJ>1 and VarJ<q, binding the full source object, actual law and both moments.
en.impact_md: Distinguish this from F08 and this paper’s appendix signed-I display. This refutes the main J clauses without thereby refuting the appendix I variant.

issues.title: 最低阶主文 J 与附录 I 的原陈述差异
issues.problem_md: 正文Eq5写J自身矩；G2重述prose仍说J，显示式却为I并带U。Theorem2定义的U还含随x′变动的符号。
issues.evidence_md: 原两个版本均完整保留。真实最低单项式的固定参考U矩已用actual maskedLowest及Gaussian法则形式化；空支持的固定输出基线另证均值b、方差0。
issues.impact_md: 不把主文folded反例扩大为附录signed I错误，也不将最低单项式类型扩大为任意DNN完整I。

en.title: Lowest-degree main J and appendix I statements differ
en.problem_md: Main Eq. (5) states J moments; G.2 repeats J in its prose but displays I with U. Theorem2’s U also includes signs varying with x′.
en.evidence_md: Both source versions are retained completely. The actual lowest monomial’s fixed-reference U moments are formalized through maskedLowest and Gaussian laws; the empty-support fixed output baseline separately has mean b and variance0.
en.impact_md: Do not extend the main folded counterexample to the signed-I appendix clause or extend the lowest-monomial type to every complete DNN dividend.

issues.title: 一般次数的绝对幂不能全改有符号幂
issues.problem_md: 奇次幂在越过参考时与绝对幂不同，≪τ只为近似。
issues.evidence_md: π1=1复用实际最低J均值/方差反例。正确folded乘积矩有实际Gaussian L2和独立法则证明；偶数幂子域绝对值可消去。
issues.impact_md: 不将错误奇次子句扩大为所有整数次数错误。

en.title: General absolute powers cannot all become signed powers
en.problem_md: Odd powers differ from absolute powers on reference-crossing tails; ≪τ is approximate.
en.evidence_md: Degree1 uses the actual lowest-J mean and variance counterexample. Correct folded-product moments have actual Gaussian L2 and independence proofs; absolute values cancel on the even-degree subdomain.
en.impact_md: The odd-degree error is not extended to every integer degree.

issues.title: Proposition1 方差项被再次平方
issues.problem_md: 原声明方差平方，下一Eq12却使用正确方差一次。
issues.evidence_md: 真实k1 GaussianX~N(0,2)：VarX=2，打印右式4；机器绑定实际积分及方差。原乘积均值仍有效。

en.title: Proposition1 squares the variance again
en.problem_md: The original statement squares variance, while the next Eq. (12) uses variance once.
en.evidence_md: For actual k1 Gaussian X~N(0,2), VarX=2 but printed RHS4. Lean binds the actual integral and variance. The product-mean clause remains valid.
en.impact_md: The correct public product_variance does not replace the original Proposition.

issues.title: 零参考交互的触发商无定义
issues.problem_md: 作者未排U_S=0，二值短证明直接约分。
issues.evidence_md: 常数网络全部非空参考交互0；原商0/0，若当前交互变非零则不能固定零U表达。κ实际反例两个U非零，避开此域。
issues.impact_md: 有效非零域的掩码/线性适配已证明，但不隐去源零域。

en.title: Trigger quotients are undefined at zero reference dividends
en.problem_md: The author does not exclude U_S=0 before cancellation in the binary proof.
en.evidence_md: A constant network has zero nonempty reference dividends, producing0/0. A nonzero current dividend cannot be represented by a fixed zero U. Both U values in the actual kappa counterexample are nonzero.
en.impact_md: Mask and linear adapters are proved on the nonzero domain; the original zero boundary remains visible.

issues.title: G3 不触发分支的包含方向错
issues.problem_md: 严格包含S⊊T不允许找到S\T元素。
issues.evidence_md: 正确分支是S不包含于T；真实maskedGame支持律不依赖此错步。
issues.impact_md: 只修证明步骤，保留Theorem4原陈述及零U范围。

en.title: Wrong inclusion direction in the G.3 inactive branch
en.problem_md: Strict inclusion S⊊T cannot supply an element of S\T.
en.evidence_md: The correct branch is S not contained in T; the actual maskedGame support theorem avoids this erroneous step.
en.impact_md: Repair the proof step while retaining Theorem4 and its zero-U scope.

issues.title: 输入 r_i 与 b_i 局部切换
issues.problem_md: Eq21/24局部输入参考符号切换，需说明同一基线。
issues.evidence_md: 原作者式原样保留；重写一致用r_i并与输出基线b区分。
issues.impact_md: 不由记号笔误单独否定非零域的二值结论。

en.title: Local switching between input r_i and b_i
en.problem_md: Eqs. (21)/(24) switch input-reference symbols locally and require an explicit same-baseline interpretation.
en.evidence_md: The original expressions are retained; the rewrite consistently uses r_i and distinguishes output baseline b.
en.impact_md: The notation slip alone does not refute binary behavior on its nonzero domain.

issues.title: 原 Eq25 内和错用 |L|=m
issues.problem_md: 按l分组内层应|L|=l，打印最终等式不是正确关系。
issues.evidence_md: 真实N3, v=z1z2, x1,r0,m1：实际上下文平均1，打印右式0；实际Lean maskedPolynomial反例。
issues.impact_md: 不得把修过下标的公式标成原等式已证。

en.title: Eq. (25) uses the wrong inner support index |L|=m
en.problem_md: The grouped inner index must be |L|=l; the printed final equality is false.
en.evidence_md: Actual N3, v=z1z2,x1,r0,m1 gives context mean1 and printed RHS0, as verified by the maskedPolynomial counterexample.
en.impact_md: A repaired-index formula is not reported as a proof of the original equality.

issues.title: 原 Eq25 包含上下文的计数错误
issues.problem_md: 固定l个变量后应从剩余n−2−l变量选m−l。
issues.evidence_md: 实际N4,v=z1z2z3,m2平均1，修内层但保留原系数时右式2。第二机器反例独立验证。
issues.impact_md: 公共一般上下文计数与l分组恒等式及论文n−2适配已机器完成，原最后错误式仍由两个反例分别否定。

en.title: Eq. (25) miscounts contexts containing a support
en.problem_md: After fixing l variables, choose m−l from the remaining n−2−l variables.
en.evidence_md: For actual N4,v=z1z2z3,m2 the mean is1, but repairing only the inner index leaves RHS2. The second machine counterexample verifies this independently.
en.impact_md: The public general context-counting and l-grouping identities and the paper n−2 adapter are machine-verified, while the two counterexamples separately refute the original final formula.

issues.title: G5 Step3 省掉特征均值
issues.problem_md: Step2含μ_i，不能在跨特征比较无条件删除。
issues.evidence_md: 真实独立Gaussian μ=(1,2),双方差1,y1，唯一最优(1/6,1/3)，比1/2而逆方差比1。Σ=Σ²=I使记号读法一致。
issues.impact_md: 保留有效期望损失、正规方程与唯一最优；Step2须按真实方差读法及非零分母限定，主反例专门反驳Step3。

en.title: G.5 Step3 drops the feature mean
en.problem_md: Step2 includes μ_i, which cannot be deleted unconditionally across features.
en.evidence_md: Actual independent Gaussians μ=(1,2), both variances1 and y1 have unique optimum(1/6,1/3), ratio1/2 versus inverse-variance ratio1. Σ=Σ²=I removes the notation ambiguity.
en.impact_md: Retain valid expected loss, normal equations and the unique optimum; Step2 is restricted to the true-variance interpretation and nonzero denominator, and the main counterexample specifically refutes Step3.

issues.title: Σ 与 Σ² 的方差记号冲突
issues.problem_md: 字面读法真实方差σ_i^4，后文比例使用σ_i²；故Step2也只能在将σ_i²解释真实方差d_i时与有效公式一致。
issues.evidence_md: 原式保留；规范真实方差d_i。主反例取两方差1，在两个读法都否定丢μ。
issues.impact_md: 不无说明将原Σ²替换成diag真实方差。

en.title: Variance notation conflicts between Σ and Σ²
en.problem_md: The literal reading gives true variance σ_i^4, whereas later ratios use σ_i². Thus Step2 agrees with the valid formula only when σ_i² is interpreted as the true variance d_i.
en.evidence_md: Retain the original expressions and use canonical true variance d_i. The main counterexample sets both variances1, refuting omission of μ under both readings.
en.impact_md: Do not silently replace original Σ² by a true-variance diagonal.

issues.title: 跨数据不能约去变化的 |U_x|
issues.problem_md: 逐样本I=U_xC_x只给加权比值，U_x随参考x变化。
issues.evidence_md: 标准化数据±1,均值0,τ1,r0,单ReLU max(t+1/2,0),b1/2；完整Gaussian明确σ，实际单例I及literal C积分给κ_I>κ_C。全部前提实际编译。
issues.impact_md: 原等号被原模型反例否定，指标I定义本身仍保留。

en.title: Variable |U_x| cannot cancel across data averages
en.problem_md: Samplewise I=U_xC_x gives a weighted ratio, since U_x varies with reference x.
en.evidence_md: Normalized data±1,mean0,τ1,r0,single ReLU max(t+1/2,0),b1/2 and the explicit full Gaussian sigma give κ_I>κ_C for the actual singleton I and literal C integrals. All premises compile.
en.impact_md: The source equality is refuted in its model, while the I definition of the metric is retained.

issues.title: chaotic 系数未控制整体协方差
issues.problem_md: 单项J方差增长与加权I增长有额外协方差、幅值与移动系数条件。
issues.evidence_md: 完整有限和方差有所有交叉协方差；源未给删除它们的定量前提。
issues.impact_md: 保留roughly近似解释，不伪造精确普遍结论。

en.title: Chaotic coefficients do not control total covariance
en.problem_md: Component-J variance growth needs additional covariance, amplitude and moving-coefficient conditions to control weighted I.
en.evidence_md: The finite-sum variance includes every cross-covariance; no quantitative premise removes them here.
en.impact_md: Retain the rough interpretation without inventing an exact universal result.

issues.title: 条件外引与学习机制解释的缺失桥梁
issues.problem_md: 完整外引前提、学习率模型与不同频率对象的适配未在本篇给出。
issues.evidence_md: 每条人读证明明确其实际源前提和所缺桥梁；Xu段为样本空间/损失景观频率，不能套F06中间特征DFT。
issues.impact_md: 不将经验/未量化解释加强成通用Lean定理，也不宣称完整外引定理被否定。

en.title: Missing bridges in cited conditions and learning interpretations
en.problem_md: Complete cited premises, a learning-rate model and adaptations between distinct frequency objects are absent here.
en.evidence_md: Each rewrite identifies its actual source premise and missing bridge. The Xu paragraph concerns sample-space/loss-landscape frequencies, not F06’s intermediate-feature DFT.
en.impact_md: Do not strengthen empirical or unquantified interpretations into generic Lean theorems or claim refutation of a cited theorem with full premises.

issues.title: 标准差、幅值和上下文平均的零域
issues.problem_md: 源未统一指定零标准差、零平均幅值、零Jaccard并集及无上下文平均的赋值。
issues.evidence_md: 常数交互给标准差0；全零概念给幅值0和Jaccard0/0；m>n−2无合法上下文。τ0亦使原J除法无定义。
issues.impact_md: 所有有效条件范围明确保留，不用Lean的总运算约定替作者补定义。

en.title: Zero domains of standard deviations, magnitudes and context averages
en.problem_md: The source has no common value for zero standard deviation, mean magnitude, Jaccard union or an empty context average.
en.evidence_md: Constant dividends have standard deviation0; all-zero concepts have magnitude0 and Jaccard0/0; m>n−2 gives no legal contexts. Tau0 also makes the original J quotient undefined.
en.impact_md: Preserve every valid conditional domain without substituting Lean’s total-operation conventions for author definitions.
